summary.not_just_software_fix: C5 changes the online residual target, event-time gradient, and fixed coordinate mask in a mathematically explicit way.
summary.novelty_not_passed: Pretrained representations, linear online adaptation, composite tracking/prediction/leakage, history integrals, command filtering, and weight projection have primary-source precedents. The exact C5 coordinate/time realization may remain a constrained contribution, but priority and sufficiency are unresolved.
summary.publication_position: A fixed-chain discrete mechanism and conditional finite-path analysis, not a new general adaptive-control theory.

items.c5_definition: a_M = M a_f + (I-M) a_req = a_req - M r_f; y_j = ((v_n-v_j) - integral_[j,n] a_M dt)/0.01; M=diag(1,1,0).
items.prior_coverage: Neural-Fly uses measured aerodynamic residual prediction in a composite update; Jiang et al. use an exponentially forgotten history-regression prediction error. Neither reviewed source gives this exact mixed PCF reference and completed-interval label.
items.evidence: 72-scene numerical physical bridge and conditional finite-path forcing decomposition (F) support the mapping. C5-vs-C3 changes the complete fixed mask, not the label alone; NO_PRED retains the target.
items.judgment: Describe as a coordinate-matched target for this fixed PCF chain. Do not claim first use or a label-only causal benefit.

items.c5_definition: At event q, use phi_(q-1) and the now-completed interval target y_(q-1) to form phi_(q-1)(W_q^T phi_(q-1)-y_(q-1))^T; the event output uses W_q before update; n=320 has no previous interval and j=n-10 thereafter.
items.prior_coverage: Neural-Fly main Eq. (8) and discrete S4 Eqs. (18)-(19) use composite tracking/prediction adaptation; Jiang et al. Eqs. (44)-(48) use history-integral prediction plus tracking/leakage. The exact C5 10-ms velocity-increment/PCF label and event ordering differ.
items.judgment: The predictive term has finite closed-loop evidence in this fixed DEV set, with 18 regressions and a near-zero T2 mean difference. No ablation compares interval duration or alternative completed-label constructions.

items.c5_definition: M=diag(1,1,0), changing only the Z coordinate relative to C3/M111 while using the same control/plant chain.
items.judgment: Supports the fixed M110 intervention on these development scenes, not global optimality, arbitrary-axis generalization, or attribution of all C5-vs-B gains.

items.c5_definition: Apply elementwise Pi_[-60,60] once to the sum of current tracking, leakage, and delayed prediction terms.
items.prior_coverage: Jiang et al. Eq. (49) use a norm-ball weight projection. Projection-set shape is a concrete operator difference but not novelty by itself. Neural-Fly's discrete covariance update is a different stability mechanism.
items.evidence: The accepted finite-path bound covers the single projected step and its numeric residual. No DEV ablation removes projection.
items.judgment: Report the exact implementation and analysis scope; do not claim the projection is a novel or separately validated performance mechanism.

items.evidence: Accepted (B/H/F) bound, ordinary floating-point post-hoc mapping over all 72 DEV trajectories. Does not establish prior Plant stability, parameter convergence, future performance, or interval-arithmetic certification.
items.judgment: Can accompany the mechanism as a scoped analysis contribution; derivation's priority and sufficiency against related discrete adaptive-control literature remain unverified.

prior_sources.citation: O'Connell et al., Neural-Fly Enables Rapid Learning for Agile Flight in Strong Winds, Science Robotics 7(66), eabm6597 (2022), DOI 10.1126/scirobotics.abm6597.
prior_sources.reviewed_parts: Main Eqs. (7)-(9): linear coefficient control, prediction/tracking/leakage composite update; Supplement S4 Eqs. (18)-(19): discrete adaptation/covariance update.

prior_sources.scope: README describes the notebook as offline DAIML training/validation; code is useful for representation and linear-fit precedent but does not expose the complete online controller.
